text: A bird called from the reeds near the dry canal.
speaker: Narrator

text: The ordinary sound made the silence afterward worse.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag looked at the ruined shelter.
speaker: Narrator

text: If this is a gate, where is the door?
speaker: Balag

text: Ninsun considered the fields, the hidden drainage passage, and Uruk beyond them.
speaker: Narrator

text: Perhaps behind us.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Enhedu's gaze went to the wall.
speaker: Narrator

text: We crawled through a drain.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Ritual accounts often preserve function rather than architecture.
speaker: Ninsun

text: That sentence was designed to excuse anything.
speaker: Enhedu

text: It was designed to explain why old texts should not be read like building plans.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik opened his satchel.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag turned.
speaker: Narrator

text: What are you doing?
speaker: Balag

text: Checking whether the journal has decided to become useful.
speaker: Zik

text: That thing has never been useful. It has been accurate. Those are not the same.
speaker: Balag

text: Zik drew it out.
speaker: Narrator

text: The cover was dry despite the mud and rain that had soaked the satchel. The scar along its surface caught the dawn like a thin line of oil.
speaker: Narrator

text: He untied the wrapping.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun moved close enough to see.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu remained behind his shoulder.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag muttered something that sounded like a ward and might have been an insult.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik opened to the map.
speaker: Narrator

text: The page showed the descending route beneath the desert. Seven narrowing turns surrounded the dark center. The line from Uruk still extended westward across the skin.
speaker: Narrator

text: For a moment, nothing changed.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then the ink nearest the city began to fade.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun reached for the page.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik caught her wrist.
speaker: Narrator

text: Do not touch it.
speaker: Zik

text: I know.
speaker: Ninsun

text: You never behave as though you know.
speaker: Zik

text: The drawn outline of Uruk paled.
speaker: Narrator

text: Walls disappeared first.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then streets.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then the temple platforms.
speaker: Narrator

text: The last mark to vanish was the western gate, though they had not passed through it.
speaker: Narrator

text: In its place, a single vertical line darkened across the route.
speaker: Narrator

text: It ran from the top of the page to the bottom.
speaker: Narrator

text: A threshold.
speaker: Narrator

text: Beside it, letters appeared in Bel-iddin's hand.
speaker: Narrator

text: The strokes formed slowly, pressing upward through the skin as if written from the other side.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun read them aloud.
speaker: Narrator

text: First gate.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag came closer.
speaker: Narrator

text: What did it take?
speaker: Balag

text: Another word formed beneath the first.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik knew what it would say before the final mark appeared.
speaker: Narrator

text: PAID.
speaker: Bel-iddin

text: The mark in his palm went cold.
speaker: Narrator
